text:
Anika (CS): Hey team — Customer #A-998 reports their month-end invoice is ~13% higher than the dashboard total. Dashboard shows embedding credits applied and a stable plan tier, but invoice has a separate embeddings line (full price) and shows plan tier bumped for 2 days. Can we audit usage attribution for 2026-02-25 -> 2026-03-01? invoice_id=inv_3K9, account=A-998 :eyes:

Priya (Support): Thanks Anika — can you paste the invoice line IDs and a quick sample of the dashboard daily totals? Also need the usage export link from usage-bot if available.

Anika (CS): invoice lines: LN_112, LN_113. Dashboard daily totals (tokens) from their UI: 2026-02-25=12,345; 2026-02-26=10,230; 2026-02-27=11,900; 2026-02-28=13,450; 2026-03-01=2,100 (these days include embedding jobs). usage-bot, link please.

usage-bot: Usage export ready: https://s3.redwood/usage-exports/A-998/2026-02-01_2026-03-01.csv.gz (signed) — contains per-request tokens, plan_id, subscription_version, rollup_key.

Jorge (Billing): looked at invoice lines — LN_112 is standard generation tokens, LN_113 is embeddings lines charged at full rate. Billing rollups show a plan tier change on 2026-02-27 (tier_standard -> tier_business) for two days which bumped unit rates. But dashboard still shows customer's plan as tier_standard for whole window.

Sam (Eng): I'm pulling the same usage export now. Quick check: running a local aggregation to compare per-day tokens grouped by rollup_key vs. dashboard attribution. SQL snippet I used:

```
SELECT usage_day, rollup_key, plan_id, sum(tokens) AS tokens
FROM usage_events
WHERE account_id = 'A-998' AND usage_day BETWEEN '2026-02-25' AND '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY usage_day, rollup_key, plan_id
ORDER BY usage_day;
```

Sam (Eng): early result looks suspicious — there are duplicate rollup_key values for 2026-02-27 with the same plan_id but different subscription_version. One group is attributed to subscription_version=7 and the other to subscription_version=8, but downstream billing rollup job merged them incorrectly and only kept the later subscription_version, which caused those tokens to be billed under the new plan. Dashboard uses the subscription mapping table (which still shows tier_standard for those days) so they differ.

Anika (CS): So the dashboard was right and billing pipeline picked the newer subscription record and retroactively billed some tokens under the upgraded plan? Customer insists they didn't change plan until 2026-03-05.

Sam (Eng): Root cause hypothesis: rollup key canonicalization in the bill-rollup lambda uses (account_id, plan_id) but not subscription_version or effective_date, so when a late subscription update came through (subscription_version bumped), the rollup merge overwrote historical buckets. In this case an automated plan migration event was ingested with an effective_date bug — it set effective_date to 2026-02-27 for a migration that should be 2026-03-05. That moved a slice of tokens into the business tier at invoice time.

Jorge (Billing): That matches the invoice: charges for 02-27 and 02-28 show higher unit price. We need to determine magnitude and affected accounts (likely rare). For A-998 the delta = $1,240.

Priya (Support): Immediate next steps? Customer wants refund/credit now if we confirm.

Sam (Eng): Proposed mitigation: 1) fix rollup merge to include subscription_version and effective_date in the rollup key to prevent overwrites, 2) run a targeted backfill for affected accounts for the billing window (2026-02-25 -> 2026-03-01) to regenerate invoice lines, 3) add a hardstop in ingestion that rejects subscription effective_date earlier than previous versions without explicit backdate flag.

Jorge (Billing): Operational: If backfill changes invoice totals, we can issue a credit memo to inv_3K9 immediately to avoid customer impact while backfill runs. I can create credit memo CM-77 for $1,240 pending verification.

Sara (Acct): please include note for audit: reason = "rollup merge overwrote historical tokens due to subscription effective_date bug".

Anika (CS): I'll message the customer that we're investigating and will apply an interim credit. Will share timeline.

Sam (Eng): ETA: I can deploy a rollup-key fix + validation check in 6h (hotfix). Backfill to regenerate rollups for the month-end window will take ~4h afterwards for the affected shard; I'll coordinate with billing so they don't double-apply.

Jorge (Billing): I'll queue the credit now and hold invoice finalization. Also flag all invoices that used the old rollup job between 2026-02-24 and 2026-03-02 for recheck.

Priya (Support): Thanks. Assigning owners: Sam (Eng) = rollup fix + backfill, Jorge (Billing) = credit memo + invoice hold, Anika (CS) = customer comms & verification, Sara (Acct) = audit entry.

Anika (CS): Customer update sent: "We've isolated a mis-attribution bug that affected token grouping for a small number of accounts. We're applying a credit of $1,240 to your invoice immediately and will confirm once the backfill finishes. Apologies." They replied :thumbsup:.

Sam (Eng): quick debug output: found 3 other accounts with identical pattern in sample shard. I'll run full scan and post list.

usage-bot: Scan complete (shard-12): affected_accounts = [A-998, A-214, A-453] — full scan across all shards queued (ETA 2h).

Jorge (Billing): Noted. Once backfill produced corrected lines I'll attach a reconciliation report and close the credit.

Priya (Support): Closing steps checklist: - customer credited (Jorge) - backfill run & verify (Sam) - reconciled invoice lines attached (Jorge) - audit ticket updated (Sara) - customer confirmation (Anika).

Anika (CS): I'll follow up with confirmation when backfill completes. Thanks everyone :heart:
